Hello everyone! My name is Ali and I am twelve years old. I live in Almaty with my mum, my dad and my little sister. I go to school every day. My favourite subject is English because it is fun and easy. After school I play football with my friends in the park. On Saturday I visit my grandmother. She makes very good tea and cakes. I like reading books, watching cartoons and listening to music. Nice to meet you!

Passengers with small children should come to the gate first. This is the final call for passenger Timur Seitkali, travelling to Astana on Flight 215. Please go to Gate 7 immediately, the doors will close in five minutes. Thank you, and have a pleasant flight.

Good evening and here is the weather for tomorrow. In the morning it will be cold and cloudy in Astana, with a temperature of minus five degrees. In the afternoon the sun will come out, but the wind will be strong, so please wear a warm hat and gloves. In Almaty it will be warmer, about eight degrees, and there may be some light rain in the evening. On Sunday the weather will be sunny and dry everywhere. Have a nice weekend!

Boarding has already started. Passengers with small children and those who need extra help will be invited to board first, followed by business class. All other passengers will then be called by row number. Please have your boarding pass and passport ready. This is the final call for Steppe Air flight 427 to Istanbul. The gate will close at 10:45. Thank you.

Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome aboard Flight 512 from Astana to Istanbul. My name is Dana, and I will be one of your flight attendants today. Before we take off, please make sure that your seat belt is fastened, your tray table is closed and your bags are stored in the overhead lockers or under the seat in front of you. If you are sitting next to an emergency exit, please read the safety card in your seat pocket. During the flight we will serve hot meals and drinks. If you need any help, just press the call button above your seat. We wish you a pleasant journey and thank you for flying with us.

Good afternoon and welcome to the Grand Steppe Hotel. Your room is on the fourth floor, room four hundred and twelve, and the lifts are just behind me on the right. Breakfast is served from seven until half past ten in the restaurant on the ground floor. The swimming pool and the gym are open all day, and you can use them free of charge. Wi-Fi is available everywhere in the hotel; the password is written on your key card. If you would like a taxi or a table at a restaurant, just call reception and we will be happy to help. Enjoy your stay!

Boarding is now expected to begin at 10:45 from Gate 12. If you had checked in online, you would already have received a message with this information, so please make sure your phone is switched on. Passengers who have not yet passed through security are kindly asked to do so without delay. This is the final call for passenger Nurlan Seitkali, travelling to Aktau. Your bags have already been loaded, so you must have checked in, but the flight is now being held for you. Please proceed immediately to Gate 12. Thank you for flying with Steppe Air.

Welcome to Charyn Canyon, one of the most spectacular natural wonders of Kazakhstan. The canyon stretches for about one hundred and fifty kilometres, and some of its walls rise more than three hundred metres above the river. The part we are standing in is known as the Valley of Castles, because the red rock formations look like ancient towers and walls. Scientists believe these rocks have been shaped by wind and water for over twelve million years. Please stay on the marked path, drink plenty of water and keep an eye on the time, as we will meet back at the bus in exactly two hours.

Distinguished guests, colleagues and friends, it is an honour to welcome you to this year's conference on the future of education. Over the past decade, technology has transformed not only the way we learn, but also what we consider worth learning. Today, students are expected to think critically, collaborate across cultures and adapt to challenges that did not exist a few years ago. Our speakers will explore how artificial intelligence, personalised learning and language skills can open doors for young people everywhere. I encourage you to ask difficult questions, challenge assumptions and leave this event with ideas you can put into practice tomorrow.
